info.name: FieldOps - Field Service Management API
info.description:
B7A6 Assignment 7 - Field Service Management (student ID last digit 7).

HOW TO RUN

1. Select the 'FieldOps - Live' environment (or leave baseUrl as-is; it points at production).

2. Open the collection menu and choose Run collection.

3. Everything passes without typing a single value. Tokens and ids are captured automatically, and the customer registered at the start uses a unique email each run, so the collection can be replayed as often as you like.

TWO REQUESTS NEED A HUMAN, and are marked MANUAL STEP in their description:

- 01 Auth > Google social login (needs an id_token from a browser sign-in)

- 04 Profile > Upload avatar (needs a file)

ONE STEP NEEDS A BROWSER: in 10 Payment, open the checkoutUrl returned by 'Initiate a Stripe payment' and pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 (any future expiry, any CVC). The requests after it - payment status, and all of 11 Feedback - depend on that payment having settled.

THE SERVICE FLOW

A customer raises a service request against one of their sites -> a dispatcher approves it and assigns a skill-matched technician into a conflict-free slot -> the technician runs the job through a guarded status workflow and logs the parts used -> the system generates an invoice from the hours actually worked -> the customer pays through Stripe -> a signature-verified webhook confirms the payment -> the customer rates the job.

DEMO ACCOUNTS (password Admin@12345 for all)

  admin@gmail.com          ADMIN

  tech.salam@gmail.com     TECHNICIAN (hydraulics - takes the job in this run)

  tech.karim@gmail.com     TECHNICIAN (HVAC - used for the wrong-skill and ownership demos)

  corp1@apextextiles.com   CUSTOMER (a different company, for the ownership demos)

GCP social login. The id_token is obtained in a browser and verified server-side against Google's public keys, including an audience check against GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, so a token minted for another application cannot be replayed here.

To try it: open {{baseUrl}}/google-signin.html, sign in with Google, and paste the token that appears into the body above.

An existing password account with the same email is linked rather than duplicated, and a Google-only account has a null password - which is why the login and change-password endpoints both guard against it.

item.name: Approve the request -> create the work order

request.description:
One Serializable transaction: verify the technician holds the required skill, check the daily job cap, create the WorkOrder with a WO- code, flip the request to CONVERTED, and write both a history row and an audit row. Either all of that happens or none of it does.

Time-overlap is deliberately NOT checked in application code - see the 409 below.

THE HEADLINE CASE.

The same technician, a time window overlapping the job just created. An application-level "is the slot free?" check has an unavoidable race: two dispatchers can both read free and both insert. Here a Postgres exclusion constraint makes the check and the write one atomic operation, so the race cannot happen at all:

  EXCLUDE USING gist (technicianId WITH =, tstzrange(scheduledStart, scheduledEnd) WITH &&)

The violation raises SQLSTATE 23P01, which the global error handler maps to a clean 409.
A rejection reason is required and is stored on the request for the customer to read.

item.description: Skill matching, the assignment transaction, and the database-enforced double-booking conflict.

item.name: 08 Work order lifecycle

request.description: Role-scoped three ways: admin sees all, a technician sees their own jobs, a customer sees their company's.

item.name: Get one work order (with full history)

request.description: Includes the complete status history - every transition, who made it and when.
Transitions are checked against a single allowed-transitions map rather than accepting whatever status the client sends. A job cannot skip from ASSIGNED straight to COMPLETED.
Legal transition, wrong actor. Scheduling is the dispatcher's job.

item.name: 403 - a different technician touches this job

request.description:
OWNERSHIP CHECK, NOT JUST A ROLE CHECK.

The caller IS a technician, so the role guard passes. The service then compares the job's technician against the caller and refuses. Without this, every technician could drive every other technician's jobs.
Re-triggers the exclusion constraint - moving a job onto an occupied window also returns 409.
Stamps actualStart. The invoice bills from the ACTUAL times worked, not the scheduled window.

unitPrice is stored on the row rather than looked up from a price list later. An invoice must keep the price as it was on the day of the job, otherwise last year's invoice silently changes when someone edits a catalogue price.
Stamps actualEnd, which closes the billable window.
Parts can only be logged while the job is EN_ROUTE or IN_PROGRESS. Once complete, the totals are frozen.

item.description: The guarded state machine end to end, including the illegal-transition, wrong-role and wrong-technician rejections.

item.name: 09 Invoicing

request.description:
One transaction: labour hours from actualEnd - actualStart (floored at 0.5h), labour = hours x the technician's hourly rate, parts = sum(unitPrice x quantity), 15% VAT, then an INV- number from a sequence, and the work order moves to INVOICED.

All five money components are stored, not just the total, so the invoice keeps its own arithmetic even after the technician's rate changes.

item.name: 10 Payment

request.description:
Writes a Payment row in INITIATED state carrying our own transactionId, then creates a Stripe Checkout session with that id in its metadata. Each attempt is its own row, so an abandoned checkout leaves a trail and the customer can retry - which is why an Invoice has many Payments.

TO COMPLETE THE PAYMENT: open the checkoutUrl from the response, pay with test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry, any CVC. Stripe then calls the webhook.

exec: pm.test('a live Stripe checkout url was returned', () => pm.expect(d.checkoutUrl).to.include('checkout.stripe.com'));

request.description: Run this before completing checkout. The payment is INITIATED and the invoice is still DUE - nothing is marked paid until the verified webhook arrives.

Run this AFTER completing checkout in the browser.

Expect payment SUCCESS, invoice PAID with paidAt set, and the work order PAID. The gatewayRef has been replaced with the Stripe payment intent, and the raw event body is stored in gatewayPayload for reconciliation.

exec: pm.test('payment settled by the verified webhook', () => pm.expect(d.status).to.eql('SUCCESS'));

item.name: Stripe webhook (reference only - do not send)

body.raw: <raw Stripe event body - Stripe sends this, not you>

request.description:
THE ONLY PATH THAT MARKS AN INVOICE PAID.

Nothing else in the codebase writes InvoiceStatus.PAID or WorkOrderStatus.PAID, and PAID has an empty role list in the transition map, so even an admin cannot set it through the status endpoint. Payment is confirmed by Stripe, never by a client redirect.

Signature verification uses the RAW request body, which is why this one route is mounted with express.raw() ahead of express.json().

Idempotent: Stripe retries webhooks. The handler looks the payment up by our transactionId and returns early if it is already SUCCESS, and re-verifies the charged amount against the invoice total before settling, so a tampered session cannot clear a large invoice with a small charge.

Sending this request by hand always returns 400 - a hand-made body cannot carry a valid Stripe signature. That is the endpoint working correctly.

item.description: Stripe Checkout and the signature-verified, idempotent webhook that is the only path to a PAID invoice.

item.name: 11 Feedback

request.description:
Closes the service flow. One transaction inserts the rating AND recomputes the technician's ratingAvg / ratingCount, so the stored average can never drift from the rows behind it.

Requires the work order to be PAID, so run this after completing checkout.
One rating per work order, enforced by a unique constraint as well as this check.

item.name: Get the feedback for a work order

request.description: A customer sees ratings they left, a technician sees ratings they received, an admin sees all.
ratingAvg and ratingCount on the assigned technician have moved after the feedback above.

item.description: REQUIRES THE BROWSER PAYMENT STEP IN FOLDER 10. Feedback is only accepted once the work order is PAID, so these requests fail with 400 until the Stripe checkout has been completed. Run the folder manually after paying.

request.description: Filters: role, status, searchTerm across name / email / phone. Passwords are stripped at the query with Prisma's omit, so they cannot leak from this endpoint even by accident.

Takes effect on the account's very NEXT request, not when its access token expires: checkAuth re-reads the user from the database on every call, and the same transaction revokes every refresh token so the session cannot be renewed.

request.description: The token below was issued BEFORE the suspension and has not expired. It is rejected anyway - that is the database re-read doing its job.
Refused. An admin locking themselves out would need database access to recover.

item.name: 13 Validation & auth errors

request.description: Zod failures are returned as a field-by-field errors array, which is what a client needs to highlight the offending inputs.
The same message is returned for an unknown email and a wrong password, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which email addresses have accounts.

item.description: 401 / 400 / 404 cases and the field-by-field validation error shape.

item.name: 14 Session teardown

request.description:
Requires the old password, and revokes every refresh token for that user - a password change is usually prompted by a suspected compromise, so leaving other sessions alive would defeat it.

Acts on the throwaway account registered at the start of this run, so nothing shared is affected.
Stamps revokedAt on the refresh token and clears both cookies.

item.description: Run last. These change the throwaway account's password and end its session.
